inventory.google_tag: Google Tag - Config - GA4 (id 101, googtag) on Initialization - All Pages, measurement id from {{Const - GA4 ID}} = G-AB12CD34EF, which matches the GA4 web stream for https://www.example.com

plan.item: Clicks on the 'Book a demo' button in the header
plan.method: Link Click trigger filtered on Click URL contains /demo/; the button is a plain link, so no site code

plan.item: Demo bookings made in the embedded scheduling widget on /demo/
plan.method: the widget is an iframe from another domain, so Tag Manager can't see inside it. A listener tag on /demo/ waits for the widget's 'examplecal.booking_confirmed' message from https://examplecal.example and pushes generate_lead to the data layer. It fires on the confirmed booking, not on a click in the widget.

plan.item: Downloads of the pricing guide PDF
plan.method: GA4 enhanced measurement (file downloads: on) already sends file_download for .pdf links; building a tag would count each download twice

plan.item: Plays of the product tour video on the home page
plan.method: GA4 enhanced measurement (video engagement: on) sends these for YouTube embeds with JavaScript API support; no tag. The preview check confirms it, and the fix if it fails is enablejsapi=1 on the embed URL

plan.item: How far people scroll on blog posts (25, 50 and 75 percent)
plan.method: enhanced measurement already sends scroll at 90%, so only 25, 50, 75 are built: a Scroll Depth trigger limited to /blog/ pages sends the same scroll event with percent_scrolled

plan.item: The jump from the pricing page to checkout on the app domain
plan.method: add example.com and app.example.net under GA4 Admin > Data streams > www.example.com > Configure tag settings > Configure your domains. The connector has no action for this setting, so it is yours to do. For Google Ads, turn on linking across domains in 'Ads - Conversion - Linker' (id 105) with app.example.net.

plan.item: Paid plan purchases on the app's order confirmation page
plan.method: a data layer push from the app when the payment is confirmed, then a Custom Event trigger and a GA4 event tag that reads the ecommerce object. The app domain loads the same container.

parameter.value:
<script>
window.addEventListener('message', function (e) {
  if (e.origin !== 'https://examplecal.example') return;
  if (!e.data || e.data.event !== 'examplecal.booking_confirmed') return;
  window.dataLayer = window.dataLayer || [];
  window.dataLayer.push({event: 'generate_lead', lead_source: 'demo_widget'});
});
</script>

payloads.why: it sets no cookies and sends nothing, so its consent setting is 'not needed'; the consent area will list it for you to confirm. It checks the message's origin, so no other frame can fake a lead.
measurement id from {{Const - GA4 ID}}, the variable the Google tag (id 101) already uses: no second configuration tag
GA4's recommended lead event name, so it can become a key event without mapping
same event name and parameter as enhanced measurement's 90% scroll, so one GA4 report shows 25, 50, 75 and 90
reads transaction_id, value, currency and items from the ecommerce object, so no data layer variables are needed
